# Region Nordjylland

Region Nordjylland is one of the five Danish administrative health regions tracked in the ADHD-DATABASEN, the national quality register run by Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) that monitors how children, adolescents and adults with ADHD are diagnosed and treated. Across the two annual reports covering 1 April 2023 – 31 March 2024 and 1 April 2024 – 31 March 2025, Region Nordjylland appears repeatedly as a region with a distinctive, sometimes contradictory, performance profile: it posts some of the lowest patient volumes and slowest process indicators in the country, yet also leads the nation on medication-related outcome measures.

In the 2023 report, the region recorded a 16 % increase in the number of ADHD assessment pathways (udredningsforløb) over the reporting period — the smallest rise of any region, compared with 24 % in [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] and [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] [^src1]. This modest growth in caseload sits alongside capacity constraints: the region's child and adolescent psychiatry service referred roughly 50 children and young people per month to private providers during the reporting period because of capacity problems, and a significant share of these outsourced cases were ADHD assessments, a factor the region itself says skewed its data on the first three assessment indicators [^src7].

Region Nordjylland's results on individual quality indicators varied widely between the 2023 and 2024 reports. On Indicator 3 (diagnostic conferences), the region posted the *highest* regional result nationally at 34 % in the 2023 report — still far below the 90 % target, but ahead of Region Syddanmark's 10 % [^src4][^src21]. On Indicator 4 (coordinating network meetings), the region achieved only 16 % (84 of 525 pathways) [^src4], and by the 2024 report Indicator 3 results had improved only to 26 % (107 of 416) [^src10]. On Indicator 2b (diagnostic interview or environmental observation), the region reported 31 % in 2023 [^src2][^src3] rising to 39 % in 2024 [^src9]. The 2023 report also noted progress ("fremgang") in both [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] and Region Nordjylland [^src5].

The region stands out most clearly on medication and adult-treatment indicators. In the 2024 report, Region Nordjylland achieved 82 % on Indicator 6 (ADHD medication within 120 days of treatment start), the highest of any region, against a national low of 56 % in Region Sjælland [^src12][^src13]. It also recorded the country's highest result on Indicator 11 (adult medication treatment within 120 days of a package pathway start), at 85 %, compared with 37 % in Region Hovedstaden [^src17]. At the same time, the region reported the lowest share of children and young people passing their final primary-school exam before age 17 among those in ADHD treatment, alongside Region Hovedstaden showing the largest gains [^src13].

Elsewhere the picture is weaker. The region had very few pre-school children assessed in the 2023 reporting period — only 23 in total [^src2]. On Indicator 5 (psychoeducation), Nordjylland and Hovedstaden achieved 33 % and 35 % respectively in 2024 [^src12], and the region explicitly told the database that it under-registers how many patients receive psychoeducation, distorting the denominator population [^src14]. On Indicator 10 (assessment of social support needs for adults), Nordjylland recorded the lowest regional result nationally at 14 %, compared with 52 % in Region Midtjylland [^src16]. The region also reported a five-percentage-point *decline* on one educational outcome measure even as Hovedstaden's rose sharply from 54 % to 67 % [^src13], and it had the lowest confirmed-diagnosis retraction rate nationally, tied with Region Sjælland at 0 %, versus 4 % in Region Hovedstaden [^src15].

Regarding patient volumes, the 2024 report gives concrete figures for the period 1 April 2024 – 31 March 2025: Region Nordjylland recorded 416 ADHD assessment pathways, 555 child/adolescent treatment pathways, and 163 adult treatment pathways [^src18]. For comparison, Region Hovedstaden recorded 2,183 assessment pathways, 1,905 child/adolescent treatment pathways, and 311 adult treatment pathways in the same period [^src18].

The region has also submitted explanatory comments to the database's steering group. It attributes poor goal achievement in child and adolescent psychiatry to the fixed deadlines used in the indicators (90 or 120 days after pathway start), while internal analyses reportedly show that more children and young people do eventually receive the relevant procedures, just after the deadline [^src19]. For the adult population, the region says low goal achievement is primarily a registration problem rather than a clinical one [^src19]. Operationally, the region's child and adolescent psychiatry outpatient service, referred to in the data as [[boerne-ungdomspsyk-ambulatorium-nordjylland|Børne- og Ungdomspsyk. Ambulatorium]], operates under Region Nordjylland [^src7], and the region reports its results into the [[adhd-databasen|ADHD-databasen]] alongside the other four Danish regions [^src11][^src12][^src13][^src14][^src19].
